narration.full_text: Today, we're diving into a cornerstone of number theory: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic. This powerful theorem tells us something profound about how numbers are built. Simply put, it states that every integer greater than one is either a prime number itself, or it can be uniquely expressed as a product of prime numbers. Think of prime numbers as the fundamental building blocks of all other numbers. For example, the number 12 can be broken down into its prime factors: two times two times three. No matter how you factor twelve, you'll always end up with two twos and one three. This uniqueness is what makes the theorem so fundamental. It guarantees that for any composite number, there's only one set of prime factors, regardless of the order in which you find them. This concept is crucial for understanding many other areas of mathematics, including finding the HCF and LCM of numbers, which we've discussed previously. It provides the foundation for those methods.
